newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: CYCLONE WATCH NEAR COCOS ISLANDS
Tropical cyclone Pancho is intensifying as it moves closer to the Australian Territory of Cocos Islands, in the Indian Ocean.
Pancho is now a category-3 cyclone, located about 140 kilometres north-north-west of the islands, moving south at 13 kilometres an hour.
Gales with gusts of up to 100 kilometres an hour are being experienced in the island area.
Winds may become very destructive, with gusts to 190-kilometres an hour later today if the cyclone centre passes close to the islands.
POKIES BANNED AS IMMORAL IN SOUTH TASSIE
A Southern Tasmanian Council has banned poker machines branding them immoral.
Gambling machines officially arrived in Tasmania's pubs and clubs on New Year's Day, and last night the Brighton Council refused to approve 15 machines at a local tavern.
Mayor, Tony Foster says the machines would have a serious effect on the local community, which is already struggling.
LEADERS PREPARING FOR WIK TALKS WITH PM
Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge says he's pleased with the way Prime Minister John Howard is responding to the native title issue in the wake of the Wik decision.
A meeting between state and territory leaders and Mr Howard has been set down for tomorrow, and Mr Borbidge is optimistic of fruitful discussions.
Mr Borbidge says he remains convinced legislation is the only way to provide certainty for pastoral leaseholders in the wake of the High Court's Wik decision.
But he's refused to detail possible solutions being considered as a result of discussions with his counterparts in Western Australia and the Northern Territory.
MINERS GO BACK TO WORK, BUT DISPUTE STILL FESTERS
Miners at the German Creek coal mine in Central Queensland are back at work this morning after a four day strike.
About 500 miners went on strike over the sacking of a union official who allegedly abused a company official.
But they voted to return to work at a mass meeting yesterday.
The CFMEU's district secretary, Greg Betts, says the Union will bring up its poor relationship with management at a hearing this week.
But mine General Manager, Mitch Jakeman, says he stands by his comments that the dispute has occurred as a result of an ego trip by a few people.
Mr Jakeman says management's been trying to talk to these people for over a week, having spent three or four months trying to agree a communication protocol with them.
ACOSS BRANDS LAST BUDGET HARSH AND UNFAIR ON POOR
The Australian Council of Social Service says a study shows that the first Coalition budget has left the so-called unemployed household A$38 a week worse off.
ACOSS President Robert Fitzgerald says the study - by Melbourne's Institute of Applied Economic and Social Research - dispels the notion that the Government's first budget was a fair one.
Mr Fitzgerald says most people think the budget was fair because it hit high income earners hard, while letting middle income earners off reasonably lightly.
But he says the study shows how harshly low income earners were treated.
Mr Fitzgerald says he'll be releasing the ACOSS submission for the next budget this morning in Canberra, and the Government mustn't repeat its last effort.
NSW POLICE NOT HAPPY WITH PAY OFFER
The New South Wales Police Association says it's disappointed by the latest pay offer from the State Government.
Late yesterday, the Government offered police a five-per cent wage rise, worth up to 25-hundred-dollars a year for each officer.
It also promised a comprehensive pay review after the Police Royal Commission hands down its final report, flagging significant wage increases in the wake of the report.
But Phil Tunchon, President of the Association, is disappointed by the offer.
EARLY WARNING AIR DEFENCE SYSTEM ON THE WAY
British Aerospace Australia is to develop the country's first short-range aircraft detection system.
BAA has won a 10-million-dollar contract to set up five-alerting and cueing systems.
They'll give the Australian Army an all-new early warning air defence capability, which is expected to be in operation within 18-months.
